title: Start in 60 minutes
intro: Don’t read the whole notebook. Get a thin working relationship into Codex in about an hour — or take the original Cursor pack if that is still your cockpit.
promise: When you finish you have: two fail-closed boundaries, one on-demand skill, one signed pattern, and two tenure clocks. That’s enough to stop the next stupid burn.

steps.title: Download the pack
steps.why: Empty templates invite dithering. This pack is already named and filled with boring defaults you can rename.
steps.do: Download the zip (or browse the files). Unzip next to a scratch project — or into a small git repo you control.
steps.proof: You can see README.md, AGENTS.md and a .agents/skills tree on disk.

steps.title: Drop files where Codex loads them
steps.why: A harness that lives only in chat dies when the chat dies.
steps.do: Copy `AGENTS.md` and `.agents/` into your project root. Start a new Codex task so project guidance is read from the beginning and the skill is discovered.
steps.proof: Codex can name the project guidance and the example-domain-task skill.

steps.title: Rename the skill to your real job
steps.why: Generic skills don’t fire. Trigger nouns must match how you talk.
steps.do: Edit skills/example-domain-task/SKILL.md: change the name, description triggers, When/Do steps, and Proof of done to one task you do weekly.
steps.proof: You can say the trigger phrase out loud and it matches the description.

steps.title: Keep two fail-closed boundaries
steps.why: Secrets in chat and silent consequential writes are the burns that don’t forgive. The host mechanism may change; the boundary must not.
steps.do: Read the two boundaries in AGENTS.md: secrets stay out of chat, and consequential writes need a visible human decision. Keep the file short. Use Codex sandboxing and permissions as separate host controls.
steps.proof: You can explain each boundary, its decision point, and what the host enforces separately.

steps.title: Sign off one pattern
steps.why: Unsigned patterns are just opinions. Sign-off is what makes Kaizen real.
steps.do: Open patterns/WORKING-PATTERNS.md. Keep a signed-off row that matches a real failure (the pack ships lean-tool-sessions and trash-instead-of-hard-delete as examples), or replace with one of yours. Write the problem in one line.
steps.proof: The table has at least one signed-off row that matches a real incident.

steps.title: Freeze a tenure clock
steps.why: Without a start date, every demo invents a heroic timeline.
steps.do: Edit clocks.json: set harness.start to today and codex.start to the first day you used Codex on real project work.
steps.proof: Two dates you trust are on disk — not only in a slide.

steps.title: Run one real task
steps.why: The harness is only real under load.
steps.do: Ask the agent to do the skill’s task. Require the proof checklist. If it skips a gate, stop and tighten the rule — don’t shrug.
steps.proof: You have a short note of what changed and how you verified it.

steps.title: Schedule a tiny Hansei
steps.why: Without reflection the pack becomes folklore in a week.
steps.do: Put a 15-minute calendar block in seven days: keep / amend / retire on the pattern and skill. Link this site’s Learning section if you want the longer loop.
steps.proof: The calendar (or ticket) exists. You are done for today.

done.title: Done when
checks: Pack installed where Codex loads it
Two fail-closed boundaries understood (secrets; consequential writes)
At least one signed-off pattern with a real problem line
One task run with proof — not a plan alone

next: When this feels boring (good), read the Codex migration note, Playbook or Learning sections. Skip what you don’t need.
